meta.title: Vibe: Easy VM sandboxes for LLM agents on MacOS
meta.author: pdubroy

comments.author: rsalmond
comments.text:
Since the docs don't mention it anywhere, for those wondering how it works it seems to make use of the MacOS VZVirtualMachine interface.

https://developer.apple.com/documentation/virtualization

comments.author: leighmcculloch
comments.text:
The choice to use VMs instead of docker/container runtimes seems like the right tradeoffs to me as well. Afaict most of the docker runtimes mount the entire macOS home directory into the shared VM, so if the container runtime is escaped the VM is unnecessarily providing access to the entire home directory.

I built something similar to Vibe in Go for my own workflows:
https://github.com/leighmcculloch/silo

Silo uses Apple Containers (or Docker if unavailable). Needing to use macOS Tahoe isn't a concern to me personally, and I like the decisions made in its design to support Dockerfiles for building the VMs, minimal init and kernel, and the intentional focus on minimal access isolation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JvQtvbhtXmo.

comments.author: inactive-user
comments.text: I briefly explored the possibility of compiling an agent tool to WASM and running on WASI for a portable sandbox that doesn't involve container or VMs, but then saw all the hoops necessary for making networking calls from WASI (preview 2 yada yada) and ran away

comments.author: jamesgecko
comments.text:
Afaict most of the docker runtimes mount the entire macOS home directory into the shared VM


Docker Desktop has "virtual file shares" in settings under Resources -> File sharing and defaults to sharing /Users, but it's a little unclear to me what this is doing. The /Users directory doesn't appear available to me by default in any dev containers I've built.

comments.author: leighmcculloch
comments.text: My understanding is that /Users is mounted into the shared vm that all the containers are mounted in. Then only the subdirectories of /Users required are mounted into the actual containers. But, the safety of this when running untrusted workloads in the containers depend on the container setup limiting access to the shared vm. If a program inside a container can access the shared vm's disk, it'll be able to access /Users.
